title: Stop Forwarding Errors, Start Designing Them
summary: A critique of error forwarding practices and a call to design errors with explicit intent: using flat, kind-based error types for machine recovery (following Apache OpenDAL's pattern) and context-aware error frames (like the exn library) for human debugging, rather than propagating errors through generic abstractions.
when-to-read: When you're designing error types or error handling strategy for a Rust library or application, or when debugging production issues caused by uninformative error messages. This differs from articles about error *recovery* (retries, timeouts, fallbacks) or testing error paths—focus here is on error *design* and *context capture*.
